summary: Former Indian Service lookout tower on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation, Navajo County; a 1958 survey describes its steel cab; listed as gone.

facts.design: 8x8 ft galvanized steel cabin on a four-legged galvanized steel structure, 120 ft overall (1958 survey description)

access.note: On the Fort Apache Indian Reservation (tribal land). Ask the tribe before visiting.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey station description of the standing steel tower, 120 ft overall

corrections.why: The 1958 survey names it the Faught Ridge Indian Service Lookout Tower; the record's agency is a place, not the agency.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA point (34.06564, -110.07456) is about 110 m from TopoQuest's Faught Ridge Lookout locale (N34.065323, W110.075663), so it matches the lookout site. The westlookouts point (34.05782, -110.05622) is about 1.9 km away and does not match the lookout locale.

notes_for_editor: The 120 ft figure is overall height from the 1958 description, not height to the cab floor, so height_m is left out. Page spells the county 'Navaho'; TopoQuest says Navajo, and the story uses Navajo. A separate TopoQuest 'Faught Ridge' ridge entry (N34.0578, W110.0562) seen only in search results explains the westlookouts coordinates; it was not read. No source describes the site today. The permission access level is the record's editorial call, supported only by the reservation location. The 1958 description calls the tower an Indian Service lookout; a human should decide the agency wording.
